text:
maria: FYI received RedHive pen-test report in S3 (PT-784). Topline: auth bypass (low complexity, privilege escalation path), KMS policy allows principal:fine-grained-role to decrypt staging artifacts, and two gaps in our audit logging for Dedicated hosts. Need a quick triage + remediation plan and retest window.
ajohnson: grabbing the report now. can you drop the S3 path? :eyes:
maria: s3://redwood-pt/reports/PT-784/2026-03-15/report.pdf
leo: tagging in since KMS policy is involved — can someone confirm which key alias?
maria: alias/aws/redwood-staging-kms (not the production key). report shows allowance for arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/fine-grained-role in the key policy.
sre-ops: if that role is used for deploy agents we should treat as high priority. Possible exploit: create a staging snapshot, pull secrets. We should rotate the key and block role, then re-deploy.
ajohnson: agree. propose: 1) rotate and create new alias 2) patch key policy to remove that role 3) snapshot rollback window for any staging jobs that might fail. Can we do a hot-rotate?
leo: hot-rotate ok for staging but need to update kms grants used by the terraform state backend. I'll prepare the minimal policy change and a rollout plan.
sec-bot: New ticket created: PT-784-KMS-POLICY (link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/PT-784-KMS-POLICY) :page_with_curl:
maria: also two logging gaps: (a) Dedicated hosts are missing SSM session logging to S3 for interactive sessions; (b) our API gateway logged requests but the body is redacted, so tampering vector not visible. report recommends enabling session-manager plugin + switch API logs to full-body retention for incidents (with redaction rules).
ajohnson: for SSM session logging I can flip the aws:SessionManager S3 target in the org policy. Quick command to check current config: ```aws ssm get-document --name AWS-StartInteractiveCommand``` but actual target is in the ssm:Put* settings in org SCP.
leo: on the API gateway bodies, we need to ensure PII redaction remains but full-body for traces flagged as 'security' can be retained. propose: a 30 day bucket with restricted access and audit trail.
sre-ops: timeline? we can do KMS rotate + ssm logging change during an after-hours maintenance window to reduce blast radius. need owners for each action and retest slots.
maria: owners: KMS & terraform state -> leo. SSM session logging -> ajohnson. API body retention -> maria. Everyone ok with after-hours window tonight 02:00-03:30 UTC?
ajohnson: I can do that window.
leo: I can make the KMS change and update terraform. will push a canary to staging first.
sre-ops: I'll stand by for rollback and monitor metrics. @oncall please be reachable.
maria: create a retest checklist for the vendor: what we changed + evidence artifacts (key rotation logs, updated key policy diff, SSM bucket delivery logs, API body retention policy and who accessed). Also include a replay plan for staging to show exploit cannot be reproduced.
sec-bot: Evidence folder created: s3://redwood-pt/evidence/PT-784/ (ACL: internal/sec only)
ajohnson: small snippet we will add to the evidence bundle (policy diff): ```- "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/fine-grained-role"} + removed entry```
leo: terraform note: will create new kms key resource and alias, migrate state with `terraform state mv` and update providers. I'll share the exact commands in the runbook.
maria: retest ask to RedHive: 1) verify that privilege escalation path no longer yields decryption 2) validate SSM session logs include session start/end and command transcript 3) confirm API body replay shows no tampering vector. propose retest window tomorrow 10:00-12:00 UTC.
ajohnson: sending vendor note now and attaching interim evidence.
sre-ops: closing loop: if anything unexpected happens during rotation we abort and rollback to old key alias and open a postmortem.
maria: thanks team — please drop short status updates in this thread during the window. :thumbsup:
